_meta.do_not_hand_edit: This file is GENERATED ground truth extracted from Stata's own scheme and style files. Regenerate it by re-running scripts/extract_scheme_truth.py; do not hand-edit.
_meta.lineplot_vs_line: Stata keeps two per-plot line stubs apart: 'p#line' is the connecting line of twoway connected, while 'p#lineplot' is the line twoway line itself draws. They are NOT interchangeable: under s2mono, 'linepattern p#line' resolves to the inherited 'linepattern p solid' while 'linepattern p#lineplot' is solid/dash/vshortdash/..., so three overlaid twoway line plots are drawn with three different dashes. Only the s2mono branch (s2mono, s2manual, s2gmanual, stmono2, stsj, sj) declares any lineplot key, and only s2mono and s2gmanual write one themselves; for every other scheme p_lineplot_* is the p#stub->pstub->p#->p fallback result, not something the scheme wrote. 'lineplot_declared' records which case a scheme is in, per class, so a translation can tell an inherited value from a declared one instead of presenting the two alike. The indirection is in Stata's own style files: style/seriesstyle-p#line.style points a line plot's line at linestyle p#line, and style/linestyle-p#line.style then sets width/color/pattern from 'scheme p#lineplot' -- whereas style/linestyle-p#.style (the connected-plot linestyle) sets color/pattern from 'scheme p#line'. Stata documents the three keys in scheme_line_plots.sthlp, and scheme_line_plots.sthlp plus scheme_shared_plots.sthlp give the fallback: a scheme without the line-plot-specific entries uses the entries shared among all plottypes, namely 'color p#' and 'linepattern p' -- NOT 'linepattern p#line', which is a different stub.
_meta.intensity_multiplier_rule: f<=1: c' = round(255-(255-c)*f); f>1: c' = round(c/f); clamp [0,255]; round half away from zero. Verified empirically against Stata 19.5 SVG export over 24 colour/multiplier cases.
_meta.color_none: Stata colour 'none' is emitted as JSON null.
_meta.label: Per-scheme 'label' is Stata's own `label "..."' line.
_meta.directive_value: Stata's scheme.class setscheme reads a directive with `tokenize' then `args style id stylename': the value is the THIRD token, a double-quoted string is one token, and anything after the value is ignored -- scheme-sttrans.scheme's `symbolsize p small *medium' is `small' (measured: its marker radius in an SVG export equals s2color's msize(small)). The resolver tokenises the same way.
_meta.opacity: A colour token's %NN suffix is Stata's opacity (0-100). It is recorded beside the hex it belongs to, per plot, in p_colors_opacity, p_line_colors_opacity, p_bar_colors_opacity, p_mark_colors_opacity and p_lineplot_colors_opacity (None when the scheme writes none); the hex lists stay plain #rrggbb. Only sttrans uses one (every p# colour is "r g b %20"). A scalar colour with an opacity suffix has no slot and is reported in 'unresolvable' rather than dropped.
_meta.provenance: Per-scheme 'provenance' parallels 'sources': for every extracted key (one record per index for the p# cycles) {kind, directive, value, file, line[, rule][, via]}. kind 'transcribed': a Stata scheme file in the #include chain writes the very key the translation carries, and file:line is that directive (via names an axisstyle indirection, or the style file a grid literal came from). kind 'inferred': no file writes the key dash reads; the value is what Stata itself falls back to -- the documented p#stub -> pstub -> p# -> p chain, a bare class default, or the generic `color grid' -- and 'rule' says which. The shipped dash-<name>.scheme files carry the same as `* provenance:' lines between `* BEGIN provenance (WP-17)' and `* END provenance (WP-17)', one per directive.
_meta.grid_color_generic: Stata's `color grid', the generic fallback SchemeParser reads when a file has no `color major_grid'. Optional in the shipped files: checked and given provenance where a file carries it (s2color, sj), never appended.
_meta.sources: Per-scheme 'sources' records, for every extracted property, the exact '<class> <key>' directive that supplied the value after the #include chain and the p#stub->pstub->p#->p fallback were applied. '<class-default>' means the value came from a bare two-token class default line (e.g. 'intensity full'), not from a named key. Notably no Stata base scheme sets 'intensity area', so area_alpha always resolves to the intensity class default.

units.*_size.value: Stata relative size units (sztype gives the kind); pt_at_4in is that value in points on Stata's 4-inch reference graph
units.default_line_width/grid_line_width.value: Stata linewidth units, the same relative size; pt_at_4in likewise
units.*_alpha.pct: percent as written in the scheme; alpha = pct/100

relative_size.definition: help size: 'relative size, where size 100 = minimum of width and height of graph'; every official gsize-/symbolsize-*.style sets sztype relative, and linewidthstyle's numeric form is the same unit
relative_size.formula_pt: pt = value / 100 * min(graphsize x, graphsize y) [inches] * 72
relative_size.note: pt_at_4in figures use Stata's 4-inch reference (s2color is 5.5 x 4in); at a scheme's own graphsize multiply by min(x, y) / 4

gsize.dash_rule: a numeric gsize is pt = value * 2.88 (the 4-inch reference), written f'{pt:g}pt' with no minimum and no truncation; a keyword takes its pt_at_4in below

symbolsize.dash_rule: a keyword takes its pt_at_4in below; a numeric symbolsize is pt = value * 2.88; pixels anchor medium (4.4pt) at 8px, i.e. px = pt * 8 / 4.4
symbolsize.not_the_gsize_ladder: large/medium = 1.59 here vs 1.27 for gsize; small/medium = 0.68 vs 0.73

linewidth.dash_rule: a linewidth keyword or number is Stata units, px = max(units x 2.88, 0.3) x 4/3 (WP-30 P1.12b)

_meta.grid_switches: draw_major_hgrid/draw_minor_hgrid (x axis, the vertical lines at the x ticks) and draw_major_vgrid/draw_minor_vgrid (y axis, the horizontal lines) are EFFECTIVE values: twoway builds the x axis with axisstyle horizontal_default and the y axis with axisstyle vertical_default, the scheme maps each role to a style name, and style/axisstyle-<name>.style names the yesno key that is read. Per-scheme 'grid_axes' records that chain and 'sources' the key that supplied each value (economist's y axis: draw_major_nlt_vgrid / draw_minor_nlt_vgrid via vertical_nolinetick). draw_major_grid/draw_minor_grid are the bare keys as transcribed; no style file reads them.

note().note: Stata's note textbox does not read gsize note; the box is the scheme's `textboxstyle note' (small_body in s2color, reverse_big in economist, key_label in s1manual), resolved per scheme in note_textbox, note_text_size, note_text_color and note_box_fill_color

xline()/yline().note: the gridlinestyle class default's style file reads `linestyle xyline'; resolved per scheme in xyline_color, xyline_pattern and xyline_line_width

plot region border.note: plotregionstyle twoway -> areastyle twoway_plotregion -> its linestyle; resolved per scheme in plotregion_line_drawn, plotregion_line_color, plotregion_line_line_width and plotregion_line_pattern

textbox_styles.source: style/textboxstyle-<name>.style: set size scheme <name>; set color scheme <name>
